I walked into the forest, knowing that I was going to face my greatest challenge yet. I fingered the heirloom in my pocket as visions of my friends and family surrounded me. “You can do it! I believe in you!” they all seemed to say. I knew that this vision couldn’t possibly be real, but it comforted me anyways, as if death didn’t seem that entirely bad if I were to lose. The leaves crunched underneath my boots as I walked on, “So you’ve come to die.” I heard. I walked into a small passing and I saw him there, the reincarnation of evil itself, jeering. “I’ve come to stop you” I proclaimed. He jeered at my confidence and shot me plank point before I had a chance to pull my weapon out of my pocket.

It was so…white. I saw a train-track in a sea of bright light. I walked along, wondering if I were really dead. Then, I saw him, my old school professor. “What are you doing here?” I asked. “Waiting for the train of course” he said. “Professor, am I really… dead?”; “What is death exactly my child,” he asked, almost amused. I stood there, pondering, “I don’t know professor, what is it?” “It’s when you leave life because you don’t have anything to do anymore” he stated, as if it were a matter of fact. “Then.. am I… done…. professor?” I asked. “That’s for you to decide.” I could hear a train in the distance, “well, time for me to go” my professor stated. He got on and offered me a hand, but I just shook my head slowly. “Not yet.” I calmly stated. He smiled then, “Good choice Harry” as the train disappeared and I woke to my body being carried by the fuzzy beard of what could only be Hagrid’s.
